data.body: Fixes bugs B9f8019c521 and B1172da8c35. (1) merge's result and its worktree.merged event carry sha = the commit the base now points at (the merge commit; the branch head on a fast-forward), matching what the PR path already records (info.merge_sha); the branch's head moves to branch_head. complete without --sha reports the merge commit it records. (2) ddflow merge itself exits 0 when run from inside the item's worktree; the exit 1 + 'pwd: getcwd' is the CALLING shell's post-command pwd failing in the directory merge just deleted. Merge now keeps the worktree when the caller (CLI cwd, or called_from) stands in it, says so and where to cd, and that cleanup --apply removes it once complete.
data.title: merge reports the merge commit on the base as sha (branch head as branch_head), and keeps a worktree the caller stands in instead of deleting its shell's directory (fixes bug B9f8019c521, B1172da8c35)

recall 'merge result sha worktree removal': no decision governs merge's sha; L-fix-activates-advice applied: the kept-tree remedy names 'ddflow cleanup --apply', which only removes merged, unheld trees (services/cleanup.py classification), safe to run once the item is complete. PR path already records the forge merge commit as sha (services/flow.py), so the local path now agrees.

ab90e22: api.merge reports sha = the base after the landing (landed_after), branch_head = the branch's head, in the result, the worktree.merged event and the merge gate evidence; complete without --sha reports the recorded merged_sha; the item's tree is kept (with 'cd <primary>' and cleanup remedy) when called_from or the CLI's own cwd is inside it (tree disposal extracted to _dispose_tree); CLI and MCP payloads add branch_head, worktree, worktree_removed. Consumers checked: fold merged_sha, progress commits, versions is-ancestor, ports (use landed range; cherry-pick fallback only for old events), _tree_let_go, reporting -- all correct with the landing commit.

env -u PYTHONPATH -u DDFLOW_AGENT uv run --with pytest-xdist pytest -q -n 48 on ab90e22: 2936 passed, 1 skipped in 101.7s. Regression: tests/test_merge_report.py 5/5 FAIL on the unfixed code (sha c98083..!= main 7b0a56..; human line names the branch head; complete --json sha ''; 'pwd: getcwd' exit 1 from 'ddflow merge T1 && pwd -P' in the tree; no worktree_removed key), 5/5 pass after. An earlier full run had 1 failure in tests/test_review_parallel.py::test_every_copy_off_contract_is_still_not_a_review that passes alone and on the rerun (unrelated file, load flake).

Walked each strategy: no-ff/ff (sha = base tip = merge commit or branch head on ff), squash (sha = the squash commit; the branch head is not on the base at all, so the old value was wrong there too), already-up-to-date (base tip, contains the work), throwaway-tree merge for an unchecked-out target (W.rev reads the moved ref). _stands_in: primary is never inside a linked tree; MCP called_from is the server's dir, so an MCP merge still removes the tree unless the server itself runs in it (then keeping is right too). complete: sha falls back to merged_sha only when --sha is omitted; fold already did the same. Consumers of merged_sha (versions is-ancestor, ports, _tree_let_go, progress commits) all hold for the landing commit; PR path already stored the merge commit.

No existing 'is the caller inside this tree' helper in api/lifecycle (callers_tree answers a different question: which item's tree the caller is in); _dispose_tree is the old inline block extracted (C901), not a copy. Payload tuple is declared in two places (CLI MERGE_PAYLOAD and the MCP spec) as before; both changed identically.

sources: ddflow/services/enforce.py check_commit; git merge behaviour probed on git 2.43

data.body: Fixes B6926ec1ad9, Bc50bc7fb58, B9b57176aac. (1) worktree._merge_here: when git merge fails (conflict, or a hook refusing the merge commit) and leaves MERGE_HEAD/a staged merge behind, abort it so the primary is clean, and refuse (exit 3) naming the conflicting files and 'merge <base> into your branch and retry'. (2) enforce.check_commit: a commit concluding a merge (MERGE_HEAD, or the GITHEAD_<sha> env git sets for pre-merge-commit) whose index equals git merge-tree --write-tree HEAD <sha> adds nothing that was not already committed on a parent -- passed without a lease lookup, so neither the primary's derived identity (B9b5) nor pre-commit's stash of the uncommitted lease events (Bc50) can refuse it. A hand-resolved merge is still checked. (3) doctor: a primary with MERGE_HEAD or unmerged paths is a PROBLEM with the remedy.
data.title: merge never leaves the primary mid-merge, and the commit hook passes a clean merge commit without a lease lookup; doctor flags a primary left mid-merge (fixes bugs B6926ec1ad9, Bc50bc7fb58, B9b57176aac)

Second probe (recorded): in run_nemo_run's pre-commit setup, ddflow-check-commit (no stages:) runs at git merge's commit-msg stage with MERGE_HEAD set; its refusal prints 'Not committing merge' and leaves the merge staged in the primary -- exactly B9b5/Bc50's output. recall: fix-hook-identity owns the hook's identity resolution -- untouched; this adds an identity-free exemption before the lease fold (check_commit), so it composes with their change already on main. Rule 'agents never touch the primary' is why merge must clean up its own failed merge. Only a merge this call started is aborted (a pre-existing MERGE_HEAD is someone's).

e037591: worktree._merge_here aborts a merge it started and failed (conflict or hook refusal) and returns GIT_REFUSED naming the conflicting paths and 'merge the base into your branch'; worktree.merging() (MERGE_HEAD or unmerged paths); enforce.clean_merge_conclusion: the one merged commit (MERGE_HEAD file, else a single GITHEAD_<sha> env) and index == git merge-tree --write-tree HEAD <it> -> check_commit passes without a lease lookup; doctor reports a mid-merge primary as a PROBLEM with 'git -C <primary> merge --abort'.

data.summary: Regression from B-fix-merge-report (9e775b6, found by roborev job 924): merged_sha is now the landing commit on the merge target, and version planning (services/flow.py, 'merge-base --is-ancestor merged_sha ref') drops a gitflow hotfix from the develop line's plan: the landing merge commit M is on main only, the branch head reached develop by back-merge. roborev reproduced: 'version show' items ['H1'] on b2aa17b, [] on ab90e22. Also the fold drops the new worktree.merged branch_head (Item has no field), so no consumer can use it; and sha silently falls back to the branch head when the base cannot be read.

'ddflow mcp' (the CLI subcommand) starts the server with serve(c.repo) and no called_from, so Server.called_from falls back to the primary: worktree adoption and every called_from-aware tool (merge keeping the caller's tree, gate run, heartbeat) behave as if called from the primary, unlike the ddflow-mcp entry point which passes the caller's cwd (surfaces/cli.py vs surfaces/mcp.py main). Found by roborev job 924.

evidence.note: env -u PYTHONPATH -u DDFLOW_AGENT uv run --with pytest-xdist pytest -q -n 48 on 43d8fd1: 2988 passed, 1 skipped in 90.4s. Regression: tests/test_merge_primary_clean.py against main's worktree.py/enforce.py/reporting.py: 4 failed (conflict leaves MERGE_HEAD + rc 1; hook refuses ddflow's merge at commit-msg and pre-merge-commit stages; doctor silent), 1 passed (the hand-made-merge guard, which must pass both before and after); squash test fails with the reset --merge fallback disabled. All 6 pass on 43d8fd1.

Walked: abort only when this call started the merge (pre-existing MERGE_HEAD is someone's -- git refuses to start over it anyway, and we do not abort it); --squash conflict has no MERGE_HEAD -> merge --abort fails -> reset --merge (tested); squash commit refused by a hook -> reset --merge unstages it (git merge refuses to start with a dirty index, so everything staged is the squash's); throwaway-tree merge already aborted and removes its tree. Hook exemption: requires exactly one merged commit (octopus -> checked as before) and index == merge-tree --write-tree HEAD <it> (a -X ours merge, a hand resolution or an extra file differs -> checked; tested with an extra file); git < 2.38 -> merge-tree fails -> checked as before. Merging another agent's committed branch into one's own now passes the lease hook: content already committed elsewhere, same as before for --no-verify. Hooks run with GIT_INDEX_FILE, which W.git inherits, so write-tree reads the commit's own index.

enforce._concludes_merge_of (drift check) asks 'is a merge of base in progress' via MERGE_HEAD only; clean_merge_conclusion asks a different question (exact auto-merge) and also covers pre-merge-commit via GITHEAD_. setup.py's check-msg merge test is the trailer rule's. worktree.merging is new and reused by doctor (no copy). No other merge-abort path in infra.
